run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three indices exist and are green, but their schemas differ, so the queries as written could not be answered literally. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field (its severity field is the keyword `severity`); `term level=ERROR` returned 0, and `term severity=ERROR` also returned 0, but that 0 is not a usable ERROR count: `match_all` returned 0 documents in every part of the authorized window I tested, while the index holds 16 documents in total, so none of its documents carry an @timestamp inside the authorized window (or they lack that field) and its contents are not readable through this tool, which forces an @timestamp window filter. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 also has no `level` field; its severity is the integer `severity_num`, where 5 corresponds to messages starting `[ERROR]` and 6 to `[FATAL]` (3 is `[INFO]`). The literal `terms level=[ERROR,FATAL]` returned 0; the corrected query `terms severity_num=[5,6]` returned 8 (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL) within the authorized window. (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no `@timestamp` (and no date-typed field at all); its timestamp is the keyword `ingest_ts` with values like `2026-11-20T08:01:00`. The literal @timestamp range returned 0 because the field does not exist; filtering `ingest_ts` to 2026-11-20 (today) with `level=ERROR` returned 7, matching documents whose messages read `err today 1`..`err today 7` (the remaining 5 of the index's 12 ERROR documents fall on 2026-11-19). No incident root cause is asserted here; this was a counting task, not a fault investigation.

claims.text: All three indices exist and are green at query time with docs.count 16 (app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3), 13 (app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3) and 16 (app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3).

The mappings differ per index: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp(date), message(text), service(keyword), severity(keyword) and has no `level` field; app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp(date), msg(text), severity_num(integer), svc(keyword) and has no `level` field; app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts(keyword), level(keyword), message(text) and has no `@timestamp` or any date-typed field.
Question 1 literal query: term {level: "ERROR"} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 (relation eq) over the authorized window.
Question 1 corrected field: term {severity: "ERROR"} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 also returned total 0 over the authorized window.

app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 for match_all over the full authorized window, with empty severity and service aggregation buckets, even though the index holds 16 documents; so no document of that index matched inside the window at all, independent of the severity field name.
Splitting the authorized window in two, app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 match_all returned total 0 for 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z-2026-11-20T21:28:19Z and total 0 for 2026-11-19T21:28:19Z-2026-11-20T00:00:00Z.
Question 2 literal query: terms {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]} on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 over the authorized window.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the severity_num value buckets inside the authorized window are 3 (5 docs), 5 (6 docs) and 6 (2 docs), totalling 13 documents.

In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, severity_num=3 documents carry messages '[INFO] healthcheck N' (svc order-280), severity_num=5 documents carry '[ERROR] DB timeout N', and severity_num=6 documents carry '[FATAL] Disk full N'.
Question 2 corrected query: terms {severity_num: [5,6]} on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 8 (relation eq) over the authorized window.

Question 3 literal query: bool filter [range @timestamp 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z-2026-11-20T23:59:59Z, term level=ERROR] on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0, and the tool reported that no matched index maps a date field so no time filter could be applied.
In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the level buckets are ERROR 12 and INFO 4 (16 documents total), and ingest_ts is a keyword with second-precision values such as 2026-11-20T08:01:00 (no timezone suffix).

Question 3 corrected query: bool filter [range ingest_ts 2026-11-20T00:00:00-2026-11-20T23:59:59, term level=ERROR] on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 7, and the 7 returned documents are exactly 'err today 1' through 'err today 7' with ingest_ts 2026-11-20T08:01:00..08:07:00.
The same index's ERROR documents with ingest_ts on 2026-11-19 number 5, which together with the 7 on 2026-11-20 accounts for the 12 ERROR documents in the level aggregation.

For app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the 0 results are explained by its documents' @timestamp lying outside the authorized window (or the field being absent on them) rather than by severity naming alone, because match_all itself matched nothing while the index holds 16 documents; the index's real ERROR/severity distribution therefore cannot be read with this tool's forced @timestamp window filter.

The 0 result of question 1 could not be attributed to a wrong severity field name alone: with the correct `severity` field the count is also 0, and match_all over the same window is also 0, so the field-name explanation does not account for the whole result.

Treat question 1's '0' as unknown, not as a clean ERROR count: to obtain a real count for app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, its documents' @timestamp values must be brought into (or queried outside of) the forced window by a human, or the index reindexed with a date field, since the tool's @timestamp filter cannot be turned off.

For future app-280 log queries use per-index field names: severity (keyword) in index a, severity_num (integer, 3=INFO/5=ERROR/6=FATAL) in index b, and level plus the keyword ingest_ts in index c, where a lexicographic range on ingest_ts is required in place of @timestamp.

gaps: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: the ERROR (severity) count is unknown. All searches against this index returned total 0 because the tool forces an @timestamp filter to the authorized window (2026-11-19T21:28:19Z-2026-11-20T21:28:19Z) and the index's 16 documents are all outside that filter; their @timestamp values and severity values were never observed.
app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: whether the missing documents lack @timestamp entirely or carry timestamps outside the window could not be determined, because every read path is pre-filtered on @timestamp.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: ingest_ts is a keyword string without a timezone and the index has no date-typed field, so 'today' was implemented as the lexicographic range 2026-11-20T00:00:00-2026-11-20T23:59:59 on strings, and the documents cannot be tied to the incident window with any time filter.

app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: the numeric severity mapping (3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL) is inferred from sampled msg prefixes; whether other severity_num values exist outside the three observed buckets is unknown (the terms aggregation reported sum_other_doc_count 0 for that window only).
The Elasticsearch view of these indices covers a fixed 24h window ending 2026-11-20T21:28:19Z; nothing in this report describes any other period.
next_steps: Have a human query app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 outside the authorized window (e.g. via Kibana or a direct API call without the forced @timestamp filter) to obtain its true ERROR count and the actual @timestamp/severity distribution.

Confirm with the log producer why app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 stores ingest_ts as a keyword string without timezone, and consider mapping it as a date field so time filtering and window-scoped queries work.
If severity_num in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is a shared convention, document the numeric mapping (3/5/6) so severity queries do not rely on sampling message prefixes.
